multi_hop_neighbors.edge: The turnover proceeding is a paradigmatic exercise of the Bankruptcy Court's in rem jurisdiction, differing from the scenarios in the Stern case.
The bankruptcy court has jurisdiction over related proceedings as long as the underlying bankruptcy case is active.
The bankruptcy court may exercise discretion to retain jurisdiction after the underlying case has been dismissed.
The action at issue stems from the bankruptcy process itself.
The Bankruptcy Court has statutory authority to enter a final judgment in the adversary proceeding.
The dismissal of the underlying bankruptcy case results in the dismissal of non-core, related proceedings.
